data.long_meaning: Pandurang is a combination of two words - 'Pandu' and 'Rang'. 'Pandu' means 'dark' and 'Rang' means 'servant'. This name signifies Lord Vishnu as the servant of his devotees. In Hindu mythology, Pandurang is a form of Lord Vishnu, who is believed to protect his devotees from all dangers. The name Pandurang carries the meaning “Lord Vishnu's servant” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Pandurang usually hope their child will grow to embody lord vishnu's servant and live with faith, good character and purpose.

vedic_reference.note: Refers to Lord Panduranga, an incarnation of Lord Vishnu, who is believed to remove all obstacles in one's life and grant all desires.

historical_references.reference: Pandurang is an epithet of Lord Panduranga, a form of Lord Vishnu, popular in the Indian state of Maharashtra. This form of Vishnu is believed to have appeared in the Dwapara Yuga, during the time of the Mahabharata war, to protect the Pandava princes Bhima and Arjuna.

Pandurang is also revered as the presiding deity of the Pandharpur city in the Indian state of Maharashtra. The city is believed to have been founded by the sage Agastya in the 3rd century CE, and the temple of Panduranga is one of the most famous temples dedicated to Lord Vishnu in Maharashtra.
